Let \theta=\arcsin\left(\dfrac{u}{6}\right). The argument is positive, so \theta is an acute angle and can be drawn in a right triangle. Call the leg adjacent to \theta x, the leg opposite it y, and the hypotenuse r. Sine returns opposite over hypotenuse, so take y=u and r=6; then x=\sqrt{r^2-y^2}=\sqrt{36-u^2}.

By the right-triangle definitions, \sin\theta=\dfrac{y}{r}, \cos\theta=\dfrac{x}{r}, \tan\theta=\dfrac{y}{x}, \csc\theta=\dfrac{r}{y}, \sec\theta=\dfrac{r}{x}, and \cot\theta=\dfrac{x}{y}. This expression asks for the cosine of \theta, so the definition to use is \cos\theta=\dfrac{x}{r}.

With x=\sqrt{36-u^2}, y=u, and r=6, \cos\theta=\dfrac{x}{r}=\dfrac{\sqrt{36-u^2}}{6}.

Therefore \cos\left(\arcsin\left(\dfrac{u}{6}\right)\right)=\boxed{\dfrac{\sqrt{36-u^2}}{6}}.
